questions.question: 33862. Contraindication of lumbar puncture
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
Head injury with raised intracranial pressure risks brain herniation if lumbar puncture is performed.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Coma and (B) Decerebrate posturing → may be clinical signs of raised ICP but not absolute contraindications unless associated with mass effect.
 (D) Mole on site → relative contraindication, risk of infection but less critical.

? Imaging is advised before LP in suspected raised ICP or head trauma.

questions.question: 33861. Which among the following is protozoal infection
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
Giardiasis is caused by Giardia lamblia, a protozoan parasite infecting the gastrointestinal tract.

❌ Other options:
 (B) Schistosomiasis → caused by trematode (fluke) worms.
 (C) Filariasis → caused by nematode worms (filarial worms).
 (D) Hydatid disease → caused by cestode (tapeworm) Echinococcus.

? Protozoa are unicellular eukaryotic parasites; others here are helminths.

questions.question: 33860. Major antibody content of the serum is
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
 The gamma (γ) fraction of serum proteins contains immunoglobulins, primarily antibodies such as IgG, the major antibody in serum.

❌ Other options:
 (A) a-I fraction → contains proteins like alpha-1 antitrypsin, not antibodies.
 (B) a-2 fraction → includes haptoglobin, not antibodies.
 (D) B fraction → not a recognized serum protein fraction.

? Serum protein electrophoresis separates proteins into fractions, with γ-globulins representing immunoglobulins.

questions.question: 33859. Biochemical disturbance occurs in fulminating hepatic failure is
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 Acute liver failure → decreased synthesis of clotting factors → prolonged prothrombin time, a sensitive marker of liver synthetic function.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Metabolic alkalosis → uncommon; usually metabolic acidosis occurs.
 (B) Hypoglycemia → can occur but less consistent.
 (C) High serum albumin → albumin decreases due to synthetic failure.

? PT prolongation is a critical prognostic factor in acute liver failure.

questions.question: 33858. Continuous capillaries are found in
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A, C) are correct:
 Cerebrum and lungs have continuous capillaries with tight junctions → restrict permeability and allow selective exchange (blood-brain barrier and alveolar capillaries).

❌ Other options:
 (B) Liver → sinusoidal capillaries, highly permeable.
 (D) Pituitary gland → fenestrated capillaries for hormone exchange.

? Continuous capillaries form selective barriers essential for organ-specific functions.

questions.question: 33857. Content of the broad ligament
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 The ovarian artery runs within the suspensory ligament, a part of the broad ligament, supplying blood to the ovary.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Testes → male gonads, not in female broad ligament.
 (B) Ovary → suspended by mesovarium, not enclosed within broad ligament.
 (C) Ureter → retroperitoneal, crosses under uterine artery, but not a content of broad ligament.

? The broad ligament contains vessels, nerves, and lymphatics supplying female reproductive organs.

questions.question: 33856. DNA viruses are
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 Parvovirus is a single-stranded DNA virus, unique among human viral pathogens.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Reovirus → double-stranded RNA virus.
 (B) Picornavirus → single-stranded RNA virus.
 (C) Orthomyxoviruses → RNA viruses (influenza).

? DNA viruses replicate in the nucleus and use host DNA polymerases.

questions.question: 33855. Continuous capillaries gaseous exchange occurs in
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
 Lungs have continuous capillaries with tight junctions that allow selective gas exchange while maintaining barrier integrity.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Thyroid gland → fenestrated capillaries.
 (C) Spleen → sinusoidal capillaries.
 (D) Bone marrow → sinusoidal capillaries.

? Continuous capillaries prevent leakage of plasma components but allow gas diffusion.

questions.question: 33854. Hemorrhagic lesions may occur
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
 Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy) impairs collagen synthesis → fragile capillaries and hemorrhagic lesions.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Vitamin B deficiencies → neurological symptoms mainly.
 (C) Retinol deficiency → causes vision problems.
 (D) Nephrotic syndrome → causes edema, not hemorrhages.

? Vitamin C is essential for hydroxylation of proline and lysine in collagen formation.

questions.question: 33853. Following predispose to the development of tuberculosis
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
 Malnutrition impairs cell-mediated immunity → increases susceptibility to tuberculosis infection and reactivation.

❌ Other options:
 (A) HLA-B27 → associated with autoimmune diseases, not TB predisposition.
 (B) Sarcoidosis → granulomatous disease mimicking TB, but not a risk factor.
 (D) Avitaminosis D → may impair immunity but less significant than malnutrition.

? Proper nutrition is critical for immune defense against mycobacterial infections.

questions.question: 33852. Linear growth is determined by
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 IGF-1 mediates the effects of growth hormone on chondrocyte proliferation and bone elongation → key regulator of linear growth.

❌ Other options:
 (A, B, C) Minerals and vitamin D are essential for bone mineralization but do not primarily regulate growth plate activity.

? IGF-1 is crucial for longitudinal bone growth during childhood and adolescence.

questions.question: 33851. Testosterone is synthesised from
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
 Testosterone is a steroid hormone synthesized from cholesterol via enzymatic pathways in Leydig cells.

❌ Other options:
 (B) Glycine → amino acid, not precursor for steroids.
 (C) Oestrogen → derived from testosterone, not precursor.
 (D) Tyrosine → precursor for catecholamines, not steroids.

? Steroid hormones share cholesterol as a common precursor.

questions.question: 33850. Excitatory cells of nervous system includes
questions.option1: Anterior horn cells of spinal cord
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
 Anterior horn cells are motor neurons that send excitatory signals to skeletal muscles → key excitatory neurons.

❌ Other options:
 (B) Ependymal cells → line ventricles, involved in CSF production, not excitatory neurons.
 (C) Microglia → immune cells of CNS, not excitatory.
 (D) Purkinje cells → inhibitory neurons in cerebellum, not excitatory.

? Anterior horn cells are alpha motor neurons essential for muscle contraction.

questions.question: 33849. Local blood vessels are dilated due to increased concentration of
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 ↑ Potassium causes vasodilation by relaxing vascular smooth muscle.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Endothelin → vasoconstrictor.
 (B) Sodium → no direct vasodilatory effect.
 (C) Calcium → vasoconstriction.

? Hyperkalemia → vasodilation.

questions.question: 33848. Causes of haematuria include
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
 Renal TB can cause granulomatous inflammation, ulceration → haematuria.

❌ Other options:
 (A) Cardiac failure rarely causes haematuria.
 (C) Pregnancy can cause transient hematuria but not pathological.
 (D) Nephrotic syndrome → proteinuria, not haematuria.

? Persistent haematuria → suspect infection, tumor, stone, TB.

questions.question: 33847. In secondary hypothyroidism
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
 Secondary hypothyroidism = pituitary failure → ↓ TSH → ↓ FT4.

❌ Other options:
 (A), (B), (D): Do not match the hormonal profile of secondary hypothyroidism.

? Low TSH + Low T4 → suspect secondary (central) hypothyroidism.

questions.question: 33846. Axillary nerve supplies the
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 Axillary nerve supplies deltoid & teres minor.

❌ Other options:
 (A), (B): Supplied by medial/lateral pectoral nerves.
 (C): Supplied by lower subscapular nerve.

? Injury → weak shoulder abduction, numbness over deltoid.

questions.question: 33845. Umbilical cord contains
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
 Umbilical cord contains 2 arteries, 1 vein → correct answer is "One umbilical vein".

❌ Other options:
 (A): Actually two arteries.
 (C), (D): Structures but not part of final cord vessels.

? Vein carries oxygenated blood from placenta to fetus.

questions.question: 33844. Which of the following hormones exhibits a diurnal rhythm in its secretion
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
 ACTH peaks in the early morning → diurnal pattern.

❌ Other options:
 (B), (C), (D): No true diurnal secretion.

? Cortisol & ACTH both show circadian rhythm.

questions.question: 33843. Rickets radiology
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
 Rickets → defective mineralization → widening of growth plate (epiphysis).

❌ Other options:
 (A) Cupping seen but widening more diagnostic.
 (B), (D): Not typical findings.

? Widened epiphysis = classic sign in active rickets.

questions.question: 33842. Spores are killed by
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
 Spores are resistant — killed by moist heat (autoclave) at 110–121°C.

❌ Other options:
 (A), (B): Insufficient.
 (D): Dry heat less effective than moist.

? Sterilization = autoclaving.

questions.question: 33841. Formation of clot is affected by
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
 Factor IX → part of intrinsic coagulation pathway → affects clot formation.

❌ Other options:
 (A), (B), (D): Not primary clotting factors.

? Factor IX deficiency = Hemophilia B.

questions.question: 33840. Which of the following organs is specially vulnerable during hemorrhagic shock?
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
 Brain → most sensitive to hypoxia → vulnerable in shock.

❌ Other options:
 (B), (C), (D): More tolerant for short periods.

? Brain injury = earliest & most dangerous in shock.

questions.question: 33839. The affinity of Hb for O2 is increased by
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
 CO binds Hb → increases apparent affinity for O₂ → left shift of curve.

❌ Other options:
 (A), (B), (C): Decrease affinity (right shift).

? CO poisoning → O₂ not released to tissues.

questions.question: 33838. Hot air oven is used for sterilization
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Swab stick → dry heat sterilization in hot air oven.

❌ Other options:
● (A), (B), (C) → usually autoclave (moist heat) or flame.

? Hot air oven → glassware, swabs, powders (not heat-labile items).

questions.question: 33837. Normal saline is
questions.option1: Capable to exert about 300 mosm/L osmotic pressure
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Normal saline = 0.9% NaCl = isotonic to plasma.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Close (~308 mOsm/L), but (C) is best.
● (B) Not hypertonic.
● (D) 9 gm/L, not 9 gm meq/L.

? Used to correct ECF deficits.

questions.question: 33836. Clearance of drug depends on
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
● Clearance (CL) = Vd × 0.693 / t½

❌ Other options:
● (B) Bioavailability affects oral dose not clearance.
● (C) Diffusion coefficient → less relevant.
● (D) Rate of absorption → affects Tmax, not clearance.

? Clearance determines steady-state levels of drug.

questions.question: 33835. In an immune mediated response, which of the following leukocytes becomes an activated macrophage.
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Monocytes → macrophages in tissues → APC, phagocytosis.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Lymphocyte → T/B cells, not macrophages.
● (B) Basophil → releases histamine.
● (C) Neutrophils → remain neutrophils.

? Monocyte → macrophage is key for innate immunity.

questions.question: 33834. In aerobic exercise there is decrease in
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
● Sweating → plasma volume ↓ during prolonged exercise.

❌ Other options:
● (B) Skin temp ↑ (vasodilation).
● (C) CBF maintained or slightly ↑.
● (D) Mean BP ↑ slightly.

? Plasma volume ↓ → need hydration during exercise.

questions.question: 33833. Insulin causes
questions.option4: entry of k into the cell
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Insulin promotes K⁺ uptake into cells (used clinically in hyperkalemia).

❌ Other options:
● (A) Glycogenolysis → inhibited.
● (B) Protein breakdown → inhibited.
● (C) Lipolysis → inhibited.

? Insulin → anabolic: ↑ glucose, K⁺, AA uptake.

questions.question: 33832. Pyramidine bases are catabolised to
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Pyrimidine breakdown → β-alanine, CO₂, and NH₃ (ammonia).

❌ Other options:
● (A) Orotic acid → intermediate in synthesis, not catabolism.
● (B) Uric acid → from purines.
● (C) Valproic acid → unrelated drug.

? Purines → uric acid; pyrimidines → CO₂, NH₃.

questions.question: 33831. In emphysema, pulmonary function test shows
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Emphysema → hyperinflation → ↑ total lung capacity (TLC), ↑ RV.

❌ Other options:
● (A) RV ↑ not ↓.
● (B) FEV1/FVC ↓ due to airflow limitation.
● (D) VC is usually ↓ or normal.

? Classic PFT: ↓ FEV1/FVC, ↑ TLC, ↑ RV.

questions.question: 33830. Substance that can easily diffuse through
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Oxygen = small, nonpolar → diffuses easily through lipid bilayer.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Glucose → large, needs transporters.
● (B) Protein → too large.
● (C) Na⁺ → needs channels.

? Lipid-soluble & small gases diffuse easily (O₂, CO₂).

questions.question: 33829. Deep cervical fascia encloses
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
● The pretracheal layer of deep cervical fascia encloses the thyroid gland, trachea, and esophagus.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Larynx → surrounded by membranes, not deep fascia.
● (C) Pineal gland → inside brain, not neck fascia.
● (D) Submandibular → enclosed by superficial fascia.

? Important: infection can spread along cervical fascia planes.

questions.question: 33828. ECG changes in hyperkalaemia
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Tall, peaked T waves → first ECG sign of hyperkalemia.

❌ Other options:
● (A) ST depression → not typical.
● (B) Short QRS → QRS prolongs with ↑ K⁺.
● (D) K+ level not an ECG change.

➕ Progressive ECG: tall T → wide QRS → sine wave → asystole.

questions.question: 33827. ACE inhibitor are contraindicated in
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Teratogenic in pregnancy → fetal renal damage.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Asthma → not a contraindication.
● (B) Acute HF → can be used carefully.
● (D) Diabetic nephropathy → ACE inhibitors beneficial.

➕ Avoid in pregnancy, bilateral RAS, angioedema.

questions.question: 33826. A major sign of cardiac tamponade is
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Pulsus paradoxus (↓ BP on inspiration) → classic tamponade sign.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Bradycardia → not typical.
● (B) Ventricular dilatation → not possible due to compression.
● (C) 3rd degree block → rare in tamponade.

➕ Tamponade = Beck’s triad: ↓ BP, muffled heart sounds, ↑ JVP.

questions.question: 33825. Causes of high ESR is
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Multiple myeloma → ↑ ESR due to high immunoglobulins.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Polycythemia → ↓ ESR.
● (B) Sickle cell → ↓ ESR.
● (D) Spherocytosis → not marked ESR change.

➕ High ESR = inflammation, infection, myeloma.

questions.question: 33824. Omega 3 essential fatty acid are
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
● Linoleic acid (LA) is an essential fatty acid; omega-6, but precursor to omega-3 pathway.

❌ Other options:
● (B) Carbonic acid → not a fatty acid.
● (C) Arachidonic acid → omega-6.
● (D) Oleic acid → omega-9.

➕ Omega-3 FAs (ALA, EPA, DHA) → anti-inflammatory effects.

questions.question: 33823. Jaundice within 24 hrs. of age
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
● Hemolysis from ABO incompatibility → early jaundice.

❌ Other options:
● (B) Septicemia → later onset jaundice.
● (C) Hepatitis → rare in neonates.
● (D) Spherocytosis → can cause jaundice, but not as commonly <24h as ABO.

➕ Jaundice <24h → always pathological!

questions.question: 33822. Bence-Jones proteins are
questions.option2: Found in the urine of multiple myeloma
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
● Free light chains in urine → seen in Multiple myeloma.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Heavy chain → incorrect, Bence-Jones = light chains.
● (C) Not specific for mononuclear antibody.
● (D) True: precipitate with heat, but B is more precise answer.

➕ Used to diagnose & monitor MM.

questions.question: 33821. Extra articular manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis are
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
● Bronchiolitis obliterans = rare lung manifestation in RA.

❌ Other options:
● (A) AKI → not direct RA manifestation.
● (C) Hepatic failure → not typical.
● (D) Leukoplakia → unrelated to RA.

➕ Other RA extra-articular: nodules, vasculitis, pericarditis, ILD.

questions.question: 33820. Antigen presenting cell except
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
● Neutrophils phagocytose but do not present antigen to T cells.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Macrophage → APC.
● (C) Langerhans cell → APC.
● (D) Dendritic cell → best APC.

➕ APC = express MHC class II: macrophages, B cells, dendritic cells.

questions.question: 33819. Renal cortisol of acid base balance is a function of
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● The distal tubule & collecting duct are key sites for H+ secretion and HCO₃⁻ reabsorption → acid-base regulation.

❌ Other options:
● (A) Loop of Henle → concentration of urine, not acid-base balance.
● (B) Proximal tubule → reabsorbs bulk of HCO₃⁻ but distal tubule fine-tunes pH.
● (D) Glomerulus → filtration, no active pH regulation.

➕ Distal nephron = important in compensating for acidosis/alkalosis.

questions.question: 33818. Causes of short stature include following except
questions.explain:
✅ Why (D) is correct:
● Klinefelter (XXY) → tall stature.

❌ Why others are incorrect:
● (A) Psychosocial → short stature.
● (B) Hypothyroidism → short stature.
● (C) GH deficiency → short stature.

➕ Other causes: Turner, Cushing, skeletal dysplasias.

questions.question: 33817. In basal condition, most of the energy used by cardiac muscle from metabolism of
questions.explain:
✅ Why (A) is correct:
● At rest → 70–80% energy from fatty acids.

❌ Why others are incorrect:
● (B) Glucose → minor role at rest.
● (C) Lactate → minor.
● (D) Pyruvate → intermediate, not major source.

➕ During stress/exercise → glucose & lactate ↑.

questions.question: 33816. Following muscles are involved in forceful respiration
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Scalene → elevates 1st & 2nd rib in forceful inspiration.

❌ Why others are incorrect:
● (A) Rectus → accessory in expiration, not inspiration.
● (B) Intercostals → involved but scalene = better option.
● (D) Soleus → leg muscle.

➕ Accessory inspiration: SCM, scalenes, external intercostals.

questions.question: 33815. Complete destruction of zona glomerulosa result in unable to produce
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
● Zona glomerulosa → aldosterone (mineralocorticoid).

❌ Why others are incorrect:
● (A) Adrenaline → adrenal medulla.
● (C) Cortisol → zona fasciculata.
● (D) DHEA → zona reticularis.

➕ Layers:
● G → Aldosterone
● F → Cortisol
● R → Androgens

questions.question: 33814. DNA synthesis is inhibited by
questions.explain:
✅ Why (C) is correct:
● Azathioprine → purine analog → blocks DNA synthesis.

❌ Why others are incorrect:
● (A) Prednisolone → steroid; no direct DNA block.
● (B) Chloramphenicol → inhibits protein synthesis (50S ribosome).
● (D) Chloroquine → antimalarial.

➕ Uses: Azathioprine = immunosuppressant.

questions.question: 33813. Retroperitoneal structures include
questions.explain:
✅ Why (B) is correct:
● Ascending colon = secondarily retroperitoneal.

❌ Why others are incorrect:
● (A) Transverse colon → intraperitoneal.
● (C) IVC → retroperitoneal but not an option matching colon question.
● (D) Appendix → intraperitoneal.

➕ Retroperitoneal mnemonic: SAD PUCKER.
